chunks: And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who intentionally killed another man's slave, he said: “He is made to pay his value and is given a severe beating.”
And he said regarding a man who killed his own slave: “He must free a slave, fast two consecutive months, and feed sixty needy persons; then repentance after that.”

key_terms.سِتِّينَ مِسْكِينًا: sixty needy persons to be fed
key_terms.يُعْتِقُ رَقَبَةً: he must free a slave as expiation
key_terms.يُغَرَّمُ قِيمَتَهُ: he must pay the slave's monetary value

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on intentionally killing a slave in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings for the intentional killing of a slave, distinguishing between killing another person's slave and killing one's own slave. In the first case, the killer must pay the slave's value and be severely punished; in the second, he must perform expiatory acts and then repent.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5167 - Hammad narrated from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdullah (as)

regarding a man who intentionally kills another man's slave.
Imam (as) said: "He must pay the value of the slave and be severely beaten."

And regarding a man who kills his own slave, Imam (as) said:
"He must free a slave, fast for two consecutive months, and feed sixty needy people, and then repent after that."
